exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal, elective cesarean, intrapartum cesarean)
cohort: 81 babies born without major complications, aged 3 to 4 months, and their mothers (aged 20-35 years, primiparous) in Palmital and Ourinhos, São Paulo, Brazil
finding: Mothers who delivered vaginally demonstrated significantly better mother-child bonding, exhibiting more visual contact, responsiveness to their child's social cues, and sensitivity compared to mothers who underwent elective or intrapartum cesarean sections.
mod_finding: Compared to elective or intrapartum cesarean section, vaginal delivery was associated with increased visual contact, better response to infant social behavior, and greater maternal sensitivity, resulting in enhanced mother-child interaction.
